In this case, a claim petition is preferred by Delhi Transport Corporation (hereinafter referred as claimant) u/s 166 & 140 of Motor Vehicle Act for claiming compensation for damage to his vehicle bearing no. DL IPC 7099 (hereinafter referred as damaged vehicle), which got damaged in an accident which took place on 22.08.2020 at about 05.30 AM, near Anand Mai Marg, Bust Stop by vehicle no. PB 10DS 8945 (hereinafter referred as offending vehicle) which was driven by Sh. Vijay Shani (hereinafter referred as driver/ R-1) and owned by Sh.
Jaspal Singh Chandhok (hereinafter referred as R-2/ owner) and insured with Reliance General Insurance Company (hereinafter referred as R-3/ Insurance Company) seeking compensation for about Rs. 3,66,165/- along with interest at 15 % per annum.

2. Brief facts of the case are that in the morning of 22.08.2020, while bus bearing no. DL 1PC 7099 was running on Bus Route no. 511 from Badarpur to Dhaula Kuan, it was hit by offending vehicle from back side at Anand Mani Marg Bus Stop,
Near Red Light towrds Crown Plaza.
The driver of such offending vehicle was apprehended by staff of damaged bus who disclosed his name as Vijay Shani.
PCR was called by driver of MACT No. 417/2021 Delhi Transport Corporation Vs. Vijay Shani & Ors.

On the basis of pleadings of the parties, evidence adduced and arguments addressed, issue-wise findings are as under:-
ISSUE NO.1 (I) Whether the damaged vehicle bearing no. DL 1PC 7099 (bus) has suffered damages in a road traffic accident dated 22.08.2020 involving vehicle bearing no. PB 10DS 8945 (Truck) driven by R-1, owned by R-2 and insured with R-3 due to rash and negligent driving of R-1, ? OPP 15.

It is well settled that the proceedings before the Claims Tribunal are in the nature of inquiry and the finding of rash and negligent driving by driver of the offending vehicle is to be returned only at the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
The factors noted above are sufficient to conclude MACT No. 417/2021 Delhi Transport Corporation Vs. Vijay Shani & Ors.

18. PW-2 driver of damaged bus as well as eye witness Sh Lila Dhar deposed on the line of claim petition about the mode and manner of the accident and categorically affirmed rash and negligent driving of Respondent No.1 which caused the accident.
PW-2 was cross examined by Ld. Counsel for R2 wherein denied the suggestion that the accident took place due to his own negligence.
He was neither questioned by R-1 nor by counsel for Insurance Company.
Nothing could be elicited in cross examination to contradict the affirmation made.
There is thus nothing to raise doubt upon uncontroverted affirmation made by driver of damaged bus.
